newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs, Cubans sign trade cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: Czechs, Cubans sign trade cooperation pact.

text.p: The Czech Republic and Cuba on Tuesday signed a trade cooperation agreement seeking to re-establish commercial links lost after the fall of communism in Prague in 1989, the Czech Industry and Trade Ministry said.

The agreement was signed by Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy and Cuban Foreign Trade Minister Ricardo Cabrisas in Singapore, where they are attending the World Trade Organisation's ministerial conference in Singapore.

"Through the closing of the agreement we are building the cornerstone for the further development of commercial economic relations between the Czech Republic and Cuba within new conditions which have been historically created," the ministry said in a statement.
Details of the agreement were not provided.
The ministry said that Cuba, after the 1959 communist revolution led by Fidel Castro, was former communist Czechoslovakia's largest foreign trade partner in Latin America.
Total Czech trade with Cuba, excluding Slovakia, plummeted to $2.32 billion in 1994, which was just 1.3 percent of total bilateral trade between the countries in 1989.
Trade turnover however began to rise again, totalling $4.94 billion in 1995, and "in 1996, the significant increase continues," the ministry said.
Dlouhy, a member of the centre-right government, visited Cuba in January for high-level talks with officials.
Ahead of that visit, Dlouhy told Cuban exiles in the United states that Czech businesses needed trade links with Havana.
